open.thesis: 84% rostered nationally and dropped by Footballers - an ownership anomaly, not a bad player. Listed WR1 for Jacksonville ahead of Meyers. PHRASING CORRECTED 14 Sep 16:40, twice now: jaguars.com publishes three FIRST-STRING receivers by alignment - Parker Washington slot, Brian Thomas Jr. left with Travis Hunter second, Jakobi Meyers right. It is not a WR1/WR2/WR3 ranking, and a summarised read of that page renders it as one, which is how this run first mis-stated it before the 13:30Z review caught it. Nobody has passed Thomas; they hold different jobs. Week 1: 3 catches for 40 in a game Jacksonville led 24-0 at half with Lawrence attempting 23 passes. He left with a shoulder and returned in the second quarter - second shoulder scare of his year, no imaging and no team statement published. REVIEWED 15 Sep: HELD. The shoulder resolved as a scare, not an injury - Liam Coen on 14 Sep: 'I fully imagine him being able to [play], no issues, just might not be able to get hit throughout the week or something.' Thomas will be limited in practice and Jacksonville expect him to play at Denver. Production still has not arrived (3 for 40) and the ownership-anomaly half of the thesis is the part still standing.
open.falsifiedIf: Target share stays under about 18% through week 3; or a Jaguars statement puts the shoulder in doubt; or Meyers out-targets him in week 2. The depth-chart clause is retained but must be read as 'loses his first-string alignment', not 'is listed second'.
open.review: Reviewed 15 Sep 17:38Z, UNRESOLVED and leaning wrong. Coen still expects him to play at Denver with limited practice. New and unfavourable: NBC has Thomas at 14 routes in Week 1, third among Jaguars receivers behind Meyers's 20. The target-share clause still runs to Week 3.
reviewHistory: Re-reviewed 15 Sep 13:10Z, UNRESOLVED and the injury half now resolved favourably. Coen's quote is the first team statement on the shoulder and it is reassuring: limited in practice, expected to play, no doubt expressed. The production half is untouched - 3 for 40 is still thin and the target-share condition still runs to week 3. The alignment-versus-ranking distinction has now caused a mis-statement in two consecutive runs; the next run should read jaguars.com directly rather than a summary of it.

open.thesis: Pittsburgh's listed RB1 and the primary passing-down back. Chem switched to full PPR, which doubles the value of the receiving edge that had made him a sit. Reviewed 14 Sep: HELD. Week 1 was 15 touches for 73 yards in a 20-13 win and Yahoo reported him taking the early lead in the Pittsburgh backfield. Warren 10.3, Tuten 9.8. No snap-share or goal-line split was retrievable, so the hold rests on touch count and one beat report rather than on usage data. REVIEWED 15 Sep: HELD, but one week from falsification and the missing data has arrived. NBC's Week 1 note, which was not retrievable yesterday, is explicit that Warren played FEWER SNAPS than Dowdle. Warren's line was 10 carries for 46 and 5 catches on 6 targets for 27. The snap half of the picture went the wrong way; the receiving half, which is what the thesis actually rested on in full PPR, held exactly. One more week like it and he is a bench player.
open.falsifiedIf: Dowdle out-touches him materially two weeks running, or Warren's target share drops below Dowdle's.
open.review: Reviewed 15 Sep 17:38Z, HELD with the same warning. Re-sourced this run: NBC has Warren on 25 of 67 snaps to Dowdle's 39; FantasyPros has Warren out-touching Dowdle 15 to 10 with 5 catches on 6 targets. DraftKings Network gives Dowdle the goal-line role. Week one of the two-week test; nothing tripped.
reviewHistory: Reviewed 15 Sep 13:10Z, HELD with a warning. The data yesterday's review recorded as unretrievable has arrived and it cuts against the thesis on snaps while confirming it on targets. Neither falsification condition has tripped - this is week one of the two-week test. The honest state is that the thesis survives on the half that matters in full PPR and is genuinely at risk on the other.

open.thesis: Reconstructed after the fact from reporting. Likely signed 3yr/$40M to follow Harbaugh from Baltimore and is the undisputed Giants TE1 and primary slot option, with Nabers coming off an ACL and a receiver room only four deep. REVIEWED 15 Sep: HELD and strengthened. 8 targets, 8 catches, 78 yards, two touchdowns in the Giants debut, with Dart saying the chemistry was immediate. Nabers returned 350 days after the ACL and the reporting has them complementary rather than competing - Nabers on Likely: 'He just catches everything.' The falsification clause about Nabers's health is therefore weaker than when written, not stronger.
open.falsifiedIf: Nabers returns to full health and Likely's route share drops below about 60%, or Theo Johnson takes the 11-personnel snaps back.
open.review: Reviewed 15 Sep 17:38Z, HELD. Re-sourced: 8 of 8 for 78 and two TDs with Dart; Nabers led the team with 9 targets. NEW FLAG: Likely played only 49% of snaps. That is snap share, not the route-share clause in falsifiedIf, so nothing tripped, but it is the number to watch at the Rams on Monday.
reviewHistory: Reviewed 15 Sep 13:10Z, HELD emphatically for the second run. The specific worry in the falsification condition - that a healthy Nabers eats the route share - is contradicted by the only reporting that addresses it directly, which has the two complementing each other in a run-first Harbaugh offence. Review after week 4 as written.

open.thesis: 8 of 9 for 138 and two scores, led Carolina in every receiving category while McMillan was quiet until garbage time. 50% rostered is an anomaly in a ten-team league. Chem priority resets weekly so the claim is free. AMENDED 14 Sep 16:40, risk raised: Coker was photographed in a walking boot Monday with an ankle tweak and ESPN has flipped him to QUESTIONABLE in the league file. He told reporters he expects to play; NBC, Yahoo and DraftKings Network all carry the same line. Carolina's first week 2 practice report lands Wednesday, AFTER the claim processes at 07:00Z. Claiming blind is accepted because Chem priority resets weekly. Sequencing: the JuiceJam trade must be sent before 07:00Z Wednesday or this claim deletes Stafford out of the offer; if the trade lands first, this claim needs no drop. RE-ISSUED 15 Sep as the same claim, evidence improved. Coker told reporters the boot was precautionary, that he does not expect to miss time, and that he plans to practise Wednesday; NBC, Yahoo, DraftKings Network and TheRX all carry it. Week 1 confirmed at 8 of 9 for 138 and two scores, 36.8 points, the top receiver of the week. The claim still processes before Carolina's Wednesday report and is still made blind on purpose, because Chem priority resets. Ordered FIRST of two claims this week.
open.falsifiedIf: Coker is limited or DNP in Carolina's Wednesday practice report, or carries a designation into Sunday; or McMillan reasserts as the clear alpha and Coker's target share falls under about 18% across weeks 2-3.
open.review: Re-issued 15 Sep 17:38Z, HELD, ordered first. Nothing reported since Monday's media session. Added this run: Bryce Young is throwing; NBC rates Atlanta's defense top 10 in Week 1 pressure rate and notes Carolina are missing two starting linemen. Stafford drop justified on the record (92.6% rostered): one-QB league, Allen is QB1, the wire holds starting QBs for Allen's Week 7 bye.
reviewHistory: Re-issued 15 Sep 13:10Z, HELD with the ankle risk slightly reduced rather than raised. Coker's own account - boot precautionary, no expected missed time, practising Wednesday - is now carried by four outlets from the same media session. RETRIEVAL TRAP for future runs: a CBS piece titled 'Panthers' Jalen Coker: Another full practice' ranks high in search and is dated December 2024, about a quadriceps injury, not this ankle. It was discarded, not used.

open.thesis: Start Likely over Pitts from week 2. This overrides ESPN's own season projection, which prefers Pitts 181.4 to 156.2 and ranks him TE7 to Likely's TE12. The override is on role: Likely is a full-time tight end for the first time on a three-year $40M deal with Nabers still managing a knee, and went 8 of 8 for 78 with two scores. Amended 14 Sep: it is NOT true that Pitts lost his role. He ran a route on 81% of Atlanta's dropbacks, tied 7th among week 1 tight ends, on one target that was an underthrown deep ball. The reason he scored nothing is the quarterback — Tua Tagovailoa ruled out Thursday with an oblique, Penix inactive and not at 100%, Cooper Rush 12 of 22 for 144. This is a close call between two intact roles, not a rout. AMENDED 14 Sep 16:40, confidence reduced again. Two things landed today. Atlanta still have no week 2 starter: Stefanski said Monday he has no updates on Tua's oblique or on Penix and no timeline, and Rapoport put Penix at 'next week or week 3'; Rush was 12/22 for 143 with 2 INTs in a 20-13 loss. That favours Likely. Against it: the Giants draw the Rams in week 2, a top-three week 2 streaming defence, while Pitts gets Carolina at home - on matchup alone the call flips. Held because who is under centre outranks matchup quality in the research order. Trigger is Atlanta's Wednesday practice report. EXECUTED 15 Sep 07:17 by the owner - Likely is in slot 6 and Pitts is on the bench, so no card was published and the validator would have rejected one. Atlanta remain unresolved: Falcons.com 11 Sep has Stefanski calling Tua's oblique day-to-day or week-to-week with no timeline and saying 'Mike will be ready when he is ready'; Yahoo 12 Sep has the club hoping Penix is ready for Week 2 but Penix saying he needs more time past the third ACL for psychological reasons. Rush went 12 of 22 for 143 with two interceptions. The quarterback question that made this call is still open.
open.falsifiedIf: Tua Tagovailoa returns and Pitts clears five targets in week 2; or Pitts out-scores Likely in two of the next three weeks; or Nabers reaches full health and Likely's route share drops below about 60%; or Theo Johnson takes the 11-personnel snaps back.
open.review: Reviewed 15 Sep 17:38Z, UNRESOLVED. Atlanta still have no named starter: Stefanski had no updates Monday, The Falcoholic expects nothing before Wednesday, and Rapoport says Penix may be too early and an oblique for a thrower is usually more than a week, which points to Cooper Rush again. That favours holding the swap.
reviewHistory: Reviewed 15 Sep 13:10Z, UNRESOLVED and now EXECUTED by the owner. Atlanta's quarterback is still not named and the reporting has moved slightly TOWARDS Pitts since yesterday - the club are hoping Penix is ready for the Week 2 home opener and Tua may return - which is the direction that would weaken this call. Held because the swap is already in effect and reversing it on a hope is churn. Wednesday's Atlanta practice report remains the trigger, and if Penix or Tua is named, Pitts's Carolina draw makes this genuinely close.

open.thesis: Consolidation two-for-one with JuiceJam (team 10). Their starting quarterback is Jared Goff at 277.8, the second-weakest starter in the league, and Stafford projects 303.4 and is the man this week's Coker claim drops for nothing. McLaurin is the sell: Washington signed Stefon Diggs in August into a room already holding Deebo Samuel and Zach Ertz, Diggs went 4/55/1 in his debut while McLaurin returned 3.4 on a 12.3 projection, and McLaurin is 30 coming off a quad injury that ended a four-year run of 17-game seasons. DeVonta Smith is their slot-4 starter and this asks for a starter — it is survivable for them only because DJ Moore sits at slot 20 on 209.0 and backfills. Computed +21.8 me / +3.8 them on season projections. Also corrects yesterday's claim that no mutually profitable trade exists in this league. RE-VERIFIED 14 Sep 16:40 against a fresh 22:16Z snapshot, not carried: recomputes to exactly +21.8 me / +3.8 them on season projections (2070.3->2092.1 and 1966.4->1970.2). On weekly projections it is -0.9 for them, so it clears on the season horizon only - the reverse of the usual one-week warning, and the likeliest reason it gets declined. Smith's role confirmed by reporting: Philadelphia's undisputed WR1 with A.J. Brown in New England, three scoreless catches in week 1. NOTE: the 22:09Z run published Chem with an empty trades array, which removed this proposal from the app while it was still live. Restored this run. URGENCY: must be sent before 07:00Z Wednesday. RE-VERIFIED 15 Sep against the 13:01Z snapshot, not carried: recomputes to exactly +21.8 me / +3.8 them (2070.3->2092.1, 1966.4->1970.2) and -0.3 for them on the week. Still live, still unaccepted, no trade activity in the log. Republished this run and promoted to the first Do-first card because the Coker claim removes Stafford from it at 07:00Z. NOTE: the exact reproduction of yesterday's numbers to the decimal, across a full week of football, is now evidence that seasonProj is a static preseason field - this trade may be priced on August's opinion.
open.falsifiedIf: They decline, or the Coker claim processes Wednesday 07:00Z and removes Stafford from the offer, whichever comes first. Also falsified if Diggs's target share collapses after week 3 and McLaurin's role recovers, which would make selling him at his lowest point the mistake.
open.review: Re-verified 15 Sep 17:38Z against the 17:16Z snapshot, HELD, still live, republished as the first card. Recomputes to exactly +21.8/+3.8 for the third run. Two corrections to the published case: (1) Goff is the LOWEST season projection among Chem starting QBs (277.8), not second-lowest as three earlier runs said; (2) Smith's Week 1 was 3 of 6 for 53 in an offense where Hurts spread 14 completions to six players, so 'volume buy' was overstated. McLaurin had 4 targets to Diggs's 9, which supports the sale. Deadline remains 07:00Z Wednesday because the Coker claim drops Stafford.
reviewHistory: Re-verified 15 Sep 13:10Z, HELD and still live for a third run. Promoted to the first Do-first card because the sequencing is now urgent rather than theoretical. The weekly figure improved from -0.9 to -0.3 for them, which is the only number that moved. The fact that nothing else moved is itself the finding, and it is recorded in the brief's cannotSee: seasonProj appears not to update, so the +21.8 may be a preseason number wearing a current date.

open.thesis: Hold Boswell over Eddy Pineiro. Pineiro is 84.9% owned on waivers at 146.8 season against Boswell's 134.6, which is a real ownership anomaly. Declined anyway: Pineiro was dropped FOR Boswell on 8 September, six days ago, and reversing a kicker slot inside a week is the exact pattern the log already carries twice as CHURN. The gap is projection-only with no reporting behind it. Boswell returned 7.0 in a 20-13 game. REVIEWED 15 Sep: HELD, and the gap is now measured rather than asserted. FantasyPros Week 2 has Boswell K15 and Pineiro K9 - six places, under a point a week - and Tyler Loop at K2 is the better target if this slot ever moves. Pineiro published to doNotChase this run so a future run does not rediscover the 84.8% ownership anomaly and reverse a seven-day-old move for the third time.
open.falsifiedIf: Boswell finishes outside the top 20 kickers across weeks 2-4, or Pittsburgh's implied team total falls below 18 for two straight weeks.
open.review: Reviewed 15 Sep 17:38Z, HELD. Comparison made on PFN's Week 2 kicker board: Loop K4, McLaughlin K6, Pineiro K12, Boswell K17. ESPN's weekly projections differ by 0.9 (Loop 8.5, Boswell 7.6), under the one-point bar, and the hold's trigger has not fired.
reviewHistory: Reviewed 15 Sep 13:10Z, HELD. The required kicker comparison was made on the Week 2 board rather than on season projections: Loop K2, Santos K4, McLaughlin K7, Pineiro K9, Boswell K15. Boswell is genuinely the worst of that group and the answer is still hold, because the slot moved seven days ago and there were two better claims competing for the same waiver run. Loop was published as the watch row with an explicit trigger so the upgrade is a decision rather than an omission.

open.thesis: Dropped this morning's ghost fallback card, which would have claimed Diggs and dropped Brian Thomas Jr. if Coker were lost. Two reasons: Thomas arrived 12 September so the churn rule closes that slot, and re-adding Diggs two days after cutting him is the reversal pattern the log punishes. No fallback claim is published this run; if Coker is lost, the claim is simply not spent. REVIEWED 15 Sep: HELD. Brian Thomas Jr. is QUESTIONABLE with the shoulder but Jacksonville expect him to play, so the condition that would reopen the slot has not fired. No fallback claim published again this run.

open.review: Reviewed 15 Sep 17:38Z, HELD. Thomas expected to play, so the slot stays closed. Diggs published as a worthALook row: 9 targets and a TD in Week 1, 36% targets per route (CBS).

open.thesis: Claim Baltimore, drop Jacksonville, on the Week 2 matchup board rather than on seasonProj. Lindy's has Baltimore 2nd hosting New Orleans and Jacksonville 9th at Denver, where the line is Denver -2.5 on a 44.5 total. Baltimore is 89.9% rostered nationally and sitting free in a ten-team league, which is the ownership-anomaly band. Chem priority resets weekly so the claim costs nothing lasting; it is ordered SECOND behind Coker, and if Coker is awarded this one most likely fails, which is an acceptable outcome because Jacksonville at 9th is a usable fallback. This directly reverses yesterday's hold, one day old - defensible only because the input the hold named moved, not because the projection was re-read. The same Baltimore defence was DECLINED in IPADE the same morning, because priority there never resets.
open.falsifiedIf: Baltimore finish outside the top 12 defence scores in Week 2, or Jacksonville finish top 5 at Denver. Either says the ranking move was noise and reversing a one-day-old hold was churn.
open.review: Reviewed 15 Sep 17:38Z, HELD but weaker. NBC's Week 2 board (published 15:45Z) puts Baltimore and Jacksonville in the same tier and says Jacksonville may sneak into the top 10; Jacksonville are without DE BJ Green. RotoBaller lists the Ravens first among Week 2 defense adds. Still a free claim, ordered second; expect a smaller gain than the morning case implied.

open.thesis: Start McLaurin in the RB/WR flex over Tuten, worth about 3.1 projected points. Not a projection-only call: Tuten took 48% of snaps and 16 touches in Week 1, but Chris Rodriguez Jr. took the short-yardage work and the only running-back red-zone carry in the game, and a back with no goal line and no passing-down role is the worst asset type in full PPR. Explicitly not in tension with selling McLaurin to JuiceJam - that offer is a judgement about sixteen weeks, this is a judgement about Sunday. If the trade lands, the card is moot and Tuten returns to the flex. Note the deliberate asymmetry with IPADE, where Tuten KEEPS the flex over MarShawn Lloyd the same morning: there the alternative's Week 1 usage could not be confirmed, here McLaurin's role is not in doubt.
open.falsifiedIf: Washington rule McLaurin out or limit him on the Week 2 report (he is 30 and coming off the quad injury that ended four straight 17-game seasons); or Jacksonville name Tuten the goal-line back, which changes what the 9.4 is made of; or the JuiceJam trade is accepted, which retires it.
open.review: Reviewed 15 Sep 17:38Z, HELD and strengthened. Rodriguez had every red-zone rush and goal-to-go snap AND ran more routes than Tuten (36% vs 40% per Zachariason; 40% vs 48% per Metz). DraftSharks expects LeQuint Allen back in the rotation. McLaurin draws a Dallas defense that allowed the most passing yards in 2025 (RotoWire).

closed.summary: One bench slot went Goedert -> Allgeier -> Likely in five days. Each step was defensible on projection; the sequence gained nothing and cost two roster moves.
Recommended dropping Kyle Monangai for Tre Tucker on 13 Sep. Monangai returned from the knee and scored 20.4; Tucker's Bowers-vacuum thesis now has a return date on it. Not acted on.

A 13 Sep run recommended adding Xavier Worthy and dropping Isaiah Likely, on the reasoning that a second TE is structurally unplayable in a RB/WR flex. Likely then scored 27.8 with two touchdowns. The structural argument was sound and the conclusion was still wrong, because it valued the slot rather than the player.

The 22:09Z 14 Sep run published Chem reporting a FINAL score of 152.9-90.4. Neither was true: 152.9 added benched Isaiah Likely's 27.8 to the starting total of 125.1, and Nicky Jam still had Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs D/ST to play on Monday night. It also shipped an empty trades array over a live proposal. Both corrected at 16:40.

Adding Isaiah Likely on 13 Sep resolved RIGHT - 27.8 with two touchdowns. Note for the pattern file: the add landed at 19:03Z, two hours after Pitts's 17:00Z kickoff, so he could never have been started in week 1. The cost of a Sunday-evening add is a whole week, not a lineup slot.

The hold-the-Jaguars-D/ST thesis is retired after one week, reversed by its own logic rather than against it. It held Jacksonville because Week 2 rankings had them 4th and Baltimore 5th. Lindy's Week 2 board now has Baltimore 2nd hosting New Orleans and Jacksonville 9th travelling to Denver. Same method, moved input, opposite answer - and the Week 1 result the hold produced was 12.0 with five sacks, so the original call was right for the week it covered. If Jacksonville finish top 5 at Denver anyway, reopen this as CHURN.

The 14 Sep worthALook row led with 'Chris Rodriguez Jr. owns the Jacksonville goal line.' Sports Illustrated's Week 1 backfield review has him at 41% of snaps, six touches and 'relegated to short-yardage duty', with one red-zone carry - the only one any Jacksonville back got. He was moved to doNotChase this run with the correction stated in whatWentWrong. The lesson is that 'owns the goal line' is a claim that needs a red-zone carry count behind it, not a role description.
